slides.title: Network operations
slides.sub: Domain 3: documentation, monitoring, recovery, services, and access
slides.say: Welcome to domain three of the Network Plus N10-009 exam: network operations. It is worth nineteen percent of the exam. We will cover documentation and change management, monitoring, disaster recovery, network services such as D H C P, D N S, and N T P, and remote access methods.

slides.title: 3.1 Documentation
head: Document
Purpose
rows: What sits in each rack unit
slides.say: Start with documentation. Network diagrams show the physical and logical layout. Rack diagrams show what sits in each rack unit. Cable maps show which cable connects which ports. I P A M tracks address space and assignments. A wireless survey and heat map shows coverage and signal strength. And an asset inventory tracks devices, owners, and licenses. Good documentation also helps you rebuild after a disaster.

slides.title: 3.1 Life cycle, change, and configuration
head: Term
Meaning
rows: Back up, wipe, remove from inventory
Request, approve, schedule, back up, implement, document
Tested, approved baseline used as the reference
slides.say: For life cycle, end of life means the vendor stops selling a product, while end of support means the vendor stops patches and help, which is when security gaps appear. Decommissioning means backing up needed data, wiping the device, and removing it from inventory and monitoring. Change management is the formal process: request, assess, get approval, schedule a maintenance window, back up first, have a rollback plan, implement, verify, and document. The production configuration is what is running. The golden configuration is the tested, approved baseline used as the reference for integrity checks.

slides.title: 3.2 Monitoring technologies
head: Tool
What it does
rows: Poll devices; agent, manager, MIB, OID; traps are alerts
NetFlow or IPFIX: who talks to whom, how much
slides.say: Objective three point two is monitoring. S N M P polls devices. An agent on the device answers a manager, the data is organized in a M I B, and each item has an O I D. Traps are alerts that devices send on their own. S N M P version three adds authentication and encryption. Flow data, such as NetFlow and I P F I X, shows who talks to whom and how much. Syslog collects logs centrally. A S I E M correlates logs and raises alerts. And a baseline records normal behavior so you can spot deviations.

slides.title: 3.2 What to watch
items: Alerts at thresholds, tied to the baseline
slides.say: Monitor interface utilization, errors, and discards. Watch device health, such as C P U, memory, and temperature. Track availability and uptime. Use environmental sensors for heat, humidity, and water. Watch for configuration changes and analyze traffic patterns. And set alerts at thresholds that are tied to your baseline.

slides.title: 3.3 Disaster recovery
head: Term
Meaning
rows: How much data loss is acceptable, measured in time
slides.say: Disaster recovery. R P O is the recovery point objective, how much data loss is acceptable, measured in time. R T O is the recovery time objective, how long recovery can take. M T T R is the mean time to repair, and M T B F is the mean time between failures. A cold site is just space and is the slowest to bring up. A warm site has equipment ready and needs some data restored. A hot site is a fully running copy, the fastest and the most expensive.

slides.title: 3.3 Redundancy and testing
items: Active-passive: a standby takes over on failure
3-2-1 rule: three copies, two media, one offsite
Tabletop exercise: walk through a scenario
Validation tests prove the plan actually works
slides.say: For redundancy, active-active means all nodes carry traffic, and active-passive means a standby takes over when the primary fails. Know the backup types: full, incremental, and differential. The three-two-one rule means three copies, on two types of media, with one offsite. A tabletop exercise walks the team through a scenario on paper, and validation tests prove that the plan really works.

slides.title: 3.4 DHCP and DNS
head: Item
Key facts
rows: Address pool, fixed address by MAC, time held
Mail server / name server / text records
slides.say: Now network services. D H C P follows four steps: discover, offer, request, and acknowledge. Know the scope, the reservation, which gives a device a fixed address by mac, and the lease. A D H C P relay forwards requests across subnets. In D N S, an A record maps a name to an I P v four address, and a quad A record maps to I P v six. A C name is an alias, and a P T R is a reverse lookup. M X names the mail server, N S names the name server, and T X T holds text, often used for email security. The hosts file is checked before D N S.

slides.title: 3.4 NTP, PTP, and IPv6 addressing
items: NTP: clock sync over UDP 123, with strata
PTP: far more precise time, for specialized networks
SLAAC: IPv6 hosts build their own address
DNSSEC: signs DNS answers to prove they are genuine
slides.say: N T P synchronizes clocks over U D P one twenty-three, using strata to describe distance from the time source. P T P is far more precise and is used on specialized networks. N T S is a secure, authenticated form of N T P. With I P v six, hosts can build their own address using slack. Encrypted D N S comes as D o H and D o T, and D N S sec signs D N S answers to prove they are genuine.

slides.title: 3.5 Access and management methods
head: Method
Remember
rows: Encrypted remote CLI on port 22; replaces Telnet
Works even when the network is down
Links two networks, usually with IPsec
Only corporate traffic vs all traffic through the VPN
A hardened host used to reach internal devices
slides.say: Last, access and management. S S H gives an encrypted command line on port twenty-two and replaces Telnet, which sends everything in cleartext. A console connection or out-of-band network works even when the production network is down. A site-to-site V P N links two networks, usually with I P sec. A client-to-site V P N connects one user. With split tunneling only corporate traffic uses the V P N, and with full tunneling all traffic does. A jump box is a hardened host used to reach internal devices, and R D P and A P I s are other ways to manage systems.

slides.title: Domain 3 recap
items: RPO vs RTO; cold, warm, hot sites
SSH over Telnet; know VPN types
slides.say: To recap domain three: know the difference between end of life and end of support, and what a golden configuration is. Know S N M P, flow data, syslog, and S I E M. Know the difference between R P O and R T O, and the cold, warm, and hot sites. Know the D H C P steps, the D N S record types, and N T P on one twenty-three. Prefer S S H over Telnet and know the V P N types. Good luck.
